name: Malkavian Cults and Madmen of Note (Libellus Sanguinis IV)

text.content:
Once numerous, the secret mystery cults of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} have dwindled in the Dark Medieval nights to three surviving orders, each built atop a foundation of smaller, ignorant cults that serve a hidden Malkavian master without knowing it. Membership is bound by three inviolable dictates: Never Reveal the Order, Protect Those of the Order, and Never Question the Order. A prospective member (a mystai, "one of the mystery") is first sponsored by an existing member, then secretly tested for months or years by the coven's mystai, and finally brought before the coven's deacon — an elder oracle who embodies a purer measure of Malkav's blood — for a final rite called the welcoming. If judged worthy, the deacon shares his blood and visions with the initiate; if not, the deacon diablerizes him outright. Each coven is led by its deacon, with mystai beneath him and initiates beneath them. Storytellers may allow active mystai to raise Virtues at current rating × 2 (instead of ×3) and may grant Road-rating advancement or bonus Willpower for meaningful participation in a cult's rites, tied to personal breakthroughs called "passing a threshold."

Ordo Aenigmatis

The Order of Enigmas seeks clarity through confrontation with the unknown — God, time, the cosmos, or Caine himself — and counts among its ranks seers, oracles, philosophers, and scientists who believe reason and mystery are two faces of the same truth. Based in the hills of Greece and moving in the orbit of the Church across Europe, the Aenigmatis have foretold the rise and fall of empires and are hunted for it. Many Aenigmatis follow the Via Caeli (Road of Heaven), the Via Ossis (Road of Bones), the Via Humanitatis, or the Via Equitum (Road of Chivalry).

Ordo Ecstasis

Where the Aenigmatis prize contemplation, the militant Ordo Ecstasis embraces the Beast itself as the key that unlocks Malkav's mystery, believing reason — not blood — is the true flaw of the Cainite condition. Its mystai indulge in revels, orgies, and battle to appease and understand the Beast, drawing artists, scholars, and warlords alike into its folds; it holds particular sway in Egypt and North Africa and among the heresies that plague the Church, making its mystai frequent blood prophets of the Cainite Heresy. Most Ecstatics follow the Via Bestae (Road of the Beast); a darker minority follow the Via Diabolis, believing their madness a gift not of Caine or Malkav but of the Devil, and a rare few tread the Via Paradocis after contact with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}.

Ordo Maleficus

Feared even by the other two orders, the Ordo Maleficus is rumored — on the evidence of the few members captured and tortured by the Aenigmatis and Ecstasis — to have fallen entirely to the Via Hyrons, the infernal road, seduced by @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} who exploit Malkavian madness for their own damnable ends. Both surviving orders have worked to extinguish it; in the current nights only rumors of the Maleficus remain, which is already too much for the sane Malkavian mind to accept.

pages.name: The Order of the Crooked Cross

text.content: A band of Cainite knights and crusaders in the service of both God and Malkav, the Order of the Crooked Cross takes its name from its symbol: a misshapen, scar-like crucifix. Its members — warriors, prophets, and wise-men, each embodying an aspect of the trinity they follow (Caine the Father, Malkav the Holy Ghost, Christ the Son) — travel the world seeking Malkav and his voice, honoring their heritage in hopes of one day redeeming their clan's cursed father from God's judgment. The order joined the Crusade to the Holy Land but has since abandoned its sword-brethren, believing the object of its search has moved on. Notable among its knights is Verro St. Germain, who welcomed the prophet Anatole into the order's company and spoke at length of its mission and mandate. A @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} seer's vision (recorded by Anatole the Prophet) suggests the order's fate: a return toward the Holy Land, a stop in a city of gold, a voice and a sign that will consume all but four of its knights until the End of Nights.

Childe of Pierre, Anatole the Prophet is a wandering @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} seer whose divine lunacy convinces him he is a herald of God's Word, sent to illuminate the mystery of Malkav's curse. Traveling in the company of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} Lucita and her Magisters as a messenger, Anatole passed through Prague — where Prince Rudolf refused him audience — and was chased by unknown hunters into the crumbling undercroft of a ruined church, where he found and fed upon (but ultimately spared) a slumbering, stone-skinned ancient Cainite whose single whispered word, "Why?", haunts him still.

His journeys eventually led him to the Skellig monastery in Bohemia, where he uncovered a Dementation forgery hidden within an illuminated manuscript, and from there to Jakab, Mystai Aenigmatis, who indoctrinated him into the Ordo Aenigmatis over a period of testing and instruction that culminated in his introduction to the deacon Maxia. Anatole's memoirs — excerpted at length in Libellus Sanguinis IV — are themselves a valuable in-character source on Malkavian history, the Tongue of Babel, the three surviving ordos, and the clan's relationships with its vampiric kin, making Anatole a useful hook for Storytellers who want a Malkavian NPC contact steeped in clan lore.

pages.name: Jakab and Maxia, Mystai and Deacon Aenigmatis

text.content:
Jakab, self-titled Mystai Aenigmatis, is the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} who tested, sponsored, and indoctrinated Anatole the Prophet into the Ordo Aenigmatis, appearing and vanishing at will along a trail of clues near the ruins of Athens before finally revealing the order's dictates and history to his initiate. Jakab is a font of clan lore — the Tongue of Babel, the legend of Malkav's Word, the myth of the Six patriarchs and their twelve, twenty, and thirty-six descendants who carry Malkav's line, and the tragedy of Saulot's death and the clan's guilty silence at the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}'s destruction. Storytellers can use Jakab as a recurring, elusive mentor figure for Malkavian player characters seeking initiation into the Aenigmatis.

Maxia is a deacon of the Ordo Aenigmatis whom Anatole sought out after Jakab's disappearance, described as one of the anointed few in whom a purer measure of Malkav's blood is said to run. As a deacon, Maxia stands at the head of her own coven of mystai and initiates, and her willingness to guide the newly initiated Anatole marks her as a useful high-level Aenigmatis contact or antagonist for chronicles touching the order.

Embraced as a child for his innocence and purity, L'Enfant Perdu ("the lost child") now holds court as prince of Antwerp, a growing seaport left to him amid the political upheaval of nearby Brussels. Dismissed as a curiosity by the dark lords of France, he in fact conceals a keen and deadly gift — inherited from his sire's own madness — for divining the weaknesses of others, which he used first to make a tool of his own sire and then to seize the throne outright. His court rivals those of Paris or London in miniature, with @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} artists and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} seneschals doting on him in hopes of favor while he plays them against one another. His madness hides a capricious, tainted nature: he has fallen to the Via Diabolis (Road of the Devil), and a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} seer's vision foretells that he will become known as "L'Enfant Terrible," condemning his own court to the Church's fires in nights to come.

pages.name: The Skellig Manuscripts and the Biblia Negra

text.content:
The monastery at Skellig in Bohemia is home to @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} monks and expert scribes who weave madness into illuminated manuscripts meant, ironically, to enlighten. Working through the Dementation power Madman's Quill, the Skellig monks subtly alter copies of classical and religious texts — Plato, Aristotle, Bibles, heretical tracts — so that the forged passages hum with a damning, infectious truth even though they are lies, unknowingly turning their readers into tools of the monastery's designs.

The Biblia Negra is the Skellig monastery's most dangerous known work: a Spanish translation, purportedly of an Arab scholar's text, written by Fra' Dolcino and fueled by his own fevered prophecies of Gehenna. It describes 67 ancient beings sleeping in earthen prisons and dreaming of a day they will reclaim the world, naming only 13 of them — disturbing echoes of the Antediluvians that convince Cainite scholars who read it that a vast conspiracy is at hand. Anyone reading the Biblia Negra who fails a Willpower roll (difficulty 8) contracts Howling @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.dfcef92487624ae8]{Lunacy} (Dementation, Level Five) and develops the derangements @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.2d3049eb96b34c63]{Paranoia} (the Ancients are real and hunting for their tombs), Delusions of Grandeur (I am their High Priest), @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.9141ccd7ef544ebb]{Obsession} (I must help them, do anything they ask), Fantasy (I had a life before the Biblia), and Amnesia (I don't know where the Biblia is). Afflicted readers eventually vanish, and the manuscript passes into the hands of another unwitting scholar.
